articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Instrumentation in Electronic Product Manufacture' (Digest No.70)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Instrumentation in Electronic Product Manufacture
IEE Colloquium on Instrumentation in Electronic Product Manufacture
abstract: The author reviews novel facilities incorporated into the 'standard' oscilloscopes. These include: autoset functions for selecting the appropriate timebase speed, input attenuation, triggering and coupling; cursor measurement facility; noise reduction and/or elimination features; availability of main./max. mode and envelope mode; waveform parameters measurements by means of automatic time and amplitude measurements; and remote control facilities.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Instrumentation in Electronic Product Manufacture
abstract: ATE (automatic test equipment) is considered as a collection of one or more test/measurement instruments that can be operated in a pre-programmed or automatic manner. The use of ATE in electronics product manufacture is discussed considering various degrees of complexity. Particular attention is paid to the Benchtop combinational tester. The use of VXIbus is also considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: CT1000: techniques for low cost analogue component testing
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Instrumentation in Electronic Product Manufacture
abstract: A need has been perceived by, Antron Electronics Ltd., for a low cost analogue integrated circuit test system that will enable test engineers, designers and Quality Assurance departments of electronic companies to evaluate, and validate, linear components. Particular emphasis is placed upon the ability of the end user to test devices under conditions that will reflect its target application. The CT1000 has been developed as an affordable alternative to specialist equipment that measures device parameters to levels of accuracy not demanded by typical goods inward verification. An IBM Personal Computer is used as the system controller, which communicates with the precision measuring circuitry by means of a plug-in I/O card.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Instrumentation in Electronic Product Manufacture
abstract: The author first considers the basic logic analyser as the general purpose design tool. The role of post processing capabilities is emphasized and the development of a modular fully interactive logic analysis system is discussed. Stimulus response measurements are dealt with and developments which support links to the CAE are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Instrumentation in Electronic Product Manufacture
abstract: The author presents an overview of VXIbus developments and discusses its impact on the ATE industry. The adoption of VXI as an industry standard for instruments on a card is considered a significant step. It brings multi-vendor respectability to modular systems, and with it the confidence that modules will become available to design smaller test systems, while, in many cases, achieving much improved performance over equivalent IEEE-488 systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
